sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'bravīn mayaḥ pārthaṃ vāsudevasya saṃnidhau prāñjaliḥ ślakṣṇayā vācā pūjayitvā punaḥ punaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Maya spoke to Pārtha in the presence of Vāsudeva, with joined palms, honouring him again and again with gentle words.

sanskrit: asmāc ca kṛṣṇāt saṃkruddhāt pāvakāc ca didhakṣataḥ tvayā trāto 'smi kaunteya brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: "By you I have been saved from this wrathful Kṛṣṇa and from Pāvaka who sought to burn me. O son of Kuntī, tell me — what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kṛtam eva tvayā sarvaṃ svasti gaccha mahāsura prītimān bhava me nityaṃ prītimanto vayaṃ ca te
english: Arjuna said: "You have already done everything. Go in peace, O great asura. Be ever well-disposed toward me, and we too shall be well-disposed toward you."

sanskrit: maya uvāca yuktam etat tvayi vibho yathāttha puruṣarṣabha prītipūrvam ahaṃ kiṃ cit kartum icchāmi bhārata
english: Maya said: "This is fitting in you, O lord, O bull among men, just as you have said. Out of affection I still wish to do something for you, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi viśvakarmā vai dānavānāṃ mahākaviḥ so 'haṃ vai tvatkṛte kiṃ cit kartum icchāmi pāṇḍava
english: "For I am the Viśvakarmā of the dānavas, their great architect. I therefore wish to do something on your behalf, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca prāṇakṛcchrād vimuktaṃ tvam ātmānaṃ manyase mayā evaṃ gate na śakṣyāmi kiṃ cit kārayituṃ tvayā
english: Arjuna said: "You consider yourself delivered from mortal peril by me. Given this, I am unable to make you do anything for me."

sanskrit: na cāpi tava saṃkalpaṃ mogham icchāmi dānava kṛṣṇasya kriyatāṃ kiṃ cit tathā pratikṛtaṃ mayi
english: "Nor do I wish your resolve to go in vain, O dānava. Let something be done for Kṛṣṇa in the same way as has been done for me."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca codito vāsudevas tu mayena bharatarṣabha muhūrtam iva saṃdadhyau kim ayaṃ codyatām iti
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus prompted by Maya, O bull of the Bhāratas, Vāsudeva reflected for a moment on what might be asked of him.

sanskrit: codayām āsa taṃ kṛṣṇaḥ sabhā vai kriyatām iti dharmarājasya daiteya yādṛśīm iha manyase
english: Kṛṣṇa then urged him: "Let a hall be built, O Daiteya, for the king Dharmarāja — such a one as you deem fitting here."

sanskrit: yāṃ kṛtāṃ nānukuryus te mānavāḥ prekṣya vismitāḥ manuṣyaloke kṛtsne 'smiṃs tādṛśīṃ kuru vai sabhām
english: "Build such an assembly hall that no human, seeing it, would be able to replicate it, and all men in this mortal world would be amazed."

sanskrit: yatra divyān abhiprāyān paśyema vihitāṃs tvayā āsurān mānuṣāṃś caiva tāṃ sabhāṃ kuru vai maya
english: "Where we might behold divine designs arranged by you — both asura and human alike — build such a hall, O Maya."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tad vākyaṃ saṃprahṛṣṭo mayas tadā vimānapratimāṃ cakre pāṇḍavasya sabhāṃ mudā
english: Accepting those words with great delight, Maya then joyfully built the assembly hall for the Pāṇḍava, resembling a celestial palace.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇaś ca pārthaś ca dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire sarvam etad yathāvedya darśayām āsatur mayam
english: Then Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha duly reported all of this to King Yudhiṣṭhira, the Dharmarāja, and presented Maya to him.

sanskrit: tasmai yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pūjāṃ yathārham akarot tadā sa tu tāṃ pratijagrāha mayaḥ satkṛtya satkṛtaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira then honoured Maya fittingly, and Maya, himself well honoured, accepted that honour with respect.

sanskrit: sa pūrvadevacaritaṃ tatra tatra viśāṃ pate kathayām āsa daiteyaḥ pāṇḍuputreṣu bhārata
english: That Daiteya then recounted here and there the ancient deeds of the gods to the sons of Pāṇḍu, O lord of the people, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa kālaṃ kaṃ cid āśvasya viśvakarmā pracintya ca sabhāṃ pracakrame kartuṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Having rested for some time and deliberated, that Viśvakarmā set about building the assembly hall for the great-souled Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: abhiprāyeṇa pārthānāṃ kṛṣṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ puṇye 'hani mahātejāḥ kṛtakautukamaṅgalaḥ
english: In accordance with the wishes of the Pārthas and the great-souled Kṛṣṇa, on an auspicious day that greatly radiant one performed the auspicious rites with festive intent.

sanskrit: tarpayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhān pāyasena sahasraśaḥ dhanaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dattvā tebhya eva ca vīryavān
english: That mighty one satisfied thousands of the foremost twice-born with rice-milk porridge, and gave them also manifold wealth.

sanskrit: sarvartuguṇasaṃpannāṃ divyarūpāṃ manoramām daśakiṣkusahasrāṃ tāṃ māpayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: He measured out on all sides that hall — endowed with the qualities of all seasons, divine in form, enchanting to the mind — at ten thousand kiṣku in extent.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uṣitvā khāṇḍavaprasthe sukhavāsaṃ janārdanaḥ pārthaiḥ prītisamāyuktaiḥ pūjanārho 'bhipūjitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Janārdana, worthy of worship and duly worshipped, had dwelt in pleasant residence at Khāṇḍavaprastha together with the Pārthas, united in affection.

sanskrit: gamanāya matiṃ cakre pitur darśanalālasaḥ dharmarājam athāmantrya pṛthāṃ ca pṛthulocanaḥ
english: That broad-eyed one, longing to see his father, resolved to depart. He then took leave of Dharmarāja and of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: vavande caraṇau mūrdhnā jagadvandyaḥ pitṛṣvasuḥ sa tayā mūrdhny upāghrātaḥ pariṣvaktaś ca keśavaḥ
english: He who is worshipped by the world bowed his head to the feet of his father's sister; she smelled the top of his head and embraced Keśava.

sanskrit: dadarśānantaraṃ kṛṣṇo bhaginīṃ svāṃ mahāyaśāḥ tām upetya hṛṣīkeśaḥ prītyā bāṣpasamanvitaḥ
english: Then the greatly glorious Kṛṣṇa saw his own sister. Approaching her, Hṛṣīkeśa went to her filled with affection and tears.

sanskrit: arthyaṃ tathyaṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ laghu yuktam anuttamam uvāca bhagavān bhadrāṃ subhadrāṃ bhadrabhāṣiṇīm
english: The blessed lord spoke to the auspicious Subhadrā, that sweet-spoken one, words that were meaningful, true, beneficial, brief, apt, and unsurpassed.

sanskrit: tayā svajanagāmīni śrāvito vacanāni saḥ saṃpūjitaś cāpy asakṛc chirasā cābhivāditaḥ
english: By her he was made to hear words conveying news of their kinsmen; she honoured him repeatedly and paid obeisance to him with bowed head.

sanskrit: tām anujñāpya vārṣṇeyaḥ pratinandya ca bhāminīm dadarśānantaraṃ kṛṣṇāṃ dhaumyaṃ cāpi janārdanaḥ
english: Having taken leave of that spirited lady and received her blessing, Janārdana the Vārṣṇeya then saw Kṛṣṇā and Dhaumya as well.

sanskrit: vavande ca yathānyāyaṃ dhaumyaṃ puruṣasattamaḥ draupadīṃ sāntvayitvā ca āmantrya ca janārdanaḥ
english: That best of men bowed to Dhaumya in the proper manner; and having comforted Draupadī and taken his leave, Janārdana

sanskrit: bhrātṝn abhyagamad dhīmān pārthena sahito balī bhrātṛbhiḥ pañcabhiḥ kṛṣṇo vṛtaḥ śakra ivāmaraiḥ
english: went, wise and mighty, to meet the brothers, accompanied by Pārtha. Kṛṣṇa, surrounded by the five brothers, shone like Śakra among the immortals.

sanskrit: arcayām āsa devāṃś ca dvijāṃś ca yadupuṃgavaḥ mālyajapyanamaskārair gandhair uccāvacair api sa kṛtvā sarvakāryāṇi pratasthe tasthuṣāṃ varaḥ
english: That bull of the Yadus worshipped both gods and twice-born with garlands, recitations, prostrations, and fragrances of various kinds. Having performed all necessary rites, that foremost among the steadfast set out.

sanskrit: svasti vācyārhato viprān dadhipātraphalākṣataiḥ vasu pradāya ca tataḥ pradakṣiṇam avartata
english: He, worthy of auspicious recitations, had the brāhmaṇas intone svasti with bowls of curds, fruits, and unbroken rice; then, having given them wealth, he circumambulated.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ ratham āsthāya tārkṣyaketanam āśugam gadācakrāsiśārṅgādyair āyudhaiś ca samanvitam
english: He mounted his golden chariot bearing the banner of Tārkṣya, swift as the wind, furnished with mace, discus, sword, Śārṅga bow, and other weapons.

sanskrit: tithāv atha ca nakṣatre muhūrte ca guṇānvite prayayau puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ sainyasugrīvavāhanaḥ
english: On an auspicious lunar day, under a favourable asterism and in a propitious muhūrta, the lotus-eyed one departed, his horses Śainy and Sugrīva drawing the chariot.

sanskrit: anvāruroha cāpy enaṃ premṇā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ apāsya cāsya yantāraṃ dārukaṃ yantṛsattamam abhīṣūn saṃprajagrāha svayaṃ kurupatis tadā
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira also mounted that chariot out of affection; and setting aside Dāruka, his excellent charioteer, the lord of the Kurus himself then took up the reins.

sanskrit: upāruhyārjunaś cāpi cāmaravyajanaṃ sitam rukmadaṇḍaṃ bṛhan mūrdhni dudhāvābhipradakṣiṇam
english: Arjuna too mounted and waved over his head a large white fly-whisk with a golden handle, turning it in a clockwise direction.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmaseno 'pi yamābhyāṃ sahito vaśī pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayau kṛṣṇam ṛtvik paurajanair vṛtaḥ
english: Likewise Bhīmasena, self-restrained and accompanied by the twins, followed behind Kṛṣṇa, along with the officiating priests and the townspeople.

sanskrit: sa tathā bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ keśavaḥ paravīrahā anugamyamānaḥ śuśubhe śiṣyair iva guruḥ priyaiḥ
english: Keśava, slayer of enemy heroes, being followed in this manner by the brothers, shone resplendent like a beloved teacher followed by his devoted pupils.

sanskrit: pārtham āmantrya govindaḥ pariṣvajya ca pīḍitam yudhiṣṭhiraṃ pūjayitvā bhīmasenaṃ yamau tathā
english: Govinda took leave of Pārtha and embraced him tightly; he honoured Yudhiṣṭhira, and Bhīmasena and the twins likewise.

sanskrit: pariṣvakto bhṛśaṃ tābhyāṃ yamābhyām abhivāditaḥ tatas taiḥ saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā yathāvan madhusūdanaḥ
english: Tightly embraced by the two twins and saluted by them, Madhusūdana then made his farewells to all of them in the proper manner.

sanskrit: nivartayitvā ca tadā pāṇḍavān sapadānugān svāṃ purīṃ prayayau kṛṣṇaḥ puraṃdara ivāparaḥ
english: Having turned back the Pāṇḍavas together with their retinues, Kṛṣṇa departed for his own city, like a second Purandara.

sanskrit: locanair anujagmus te tam ā dṛṣṭipathāt tadā manobhir anujagmus te kṛṣṇaṃ prītisamanvayāt
english: They followed him with their eyes as far as the range of vision; then, out of love, they followed Kṛṣṇa with their minds.

sanskrit: atṛptamanasām eva teṣāṃ keśavadarśane kṣipram antardadhe śauriś cakṣuṣāṃ priyadarśanaḥ
english: Though their minds were unsated in beholding Keśava, the glorious Śauri, fair to behold, quickly vanished from their sight.

sanskrit: akāmā iva pārthās te govindagatamānasāḥ nivṛtyopayayuḥ sarve svapuraṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ syandanenātha kṛṣṇo 'pi samaye dvārakām agāt
english: Those bulls among men, the Pārthas, their minds gone with Govinda and as though unwilling, all turned back and returned to their city. And Kṛṣṇa too in his chariot reached Dvārakā in due time.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athābravīn mayaḥ pārtham arjunaṃ jayatāṃ varam āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi kṣipram eṣyāmi cāpy aham
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Maya said to Pārtha Arjuna, foremost among the victorious: "I take my leave of you; I shall go swiftly and shall return as well."

sanskrit: uttareṇa tu kailāsaṃ mainākaṃ parvataṃ prati yakṣyamāṇeṣu sarveṣu dānaveṣu tadā mayā kṛtaṃ maṇimayaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ ramyaṃ bindusaraḥ prati
english: "When all the dānavas were about to perform a sacrifice, I made a jewel-adorned vessel, beautiful, near Bindu Lake, to the north of Kailāsa toward Mount Maināka."

sanskrit: sabhāyāṃ satyasaṃdhasya yad āsīd vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ āgamiṣyāmi tad gṛhya yadi tiṣṭhati bhārata
english: "I shall come back bringing whatever was in the assembly hall of the truth-pledged Vṛṣaparvan — if it still remains there, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhāṃ kariṣyāmi pāṇḍavāya yaśasvine manaḥprahlādinīṃ citrāṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitām
english: "Then I shall build for the glorious Pāṇḍava an assembly hall delightful to the mind, wondrous, adorned with all manner of jewels."

sanskrit: asti bindusarasy eva gadā śreṣṭhā kurūdvaha nihitā yauvanāśvena rājñā hatvā raṇe ripūn suvarṇabindubhiś citrā gurvī bhārasahā dṛḍhā
english: "There at Bindu Lake, O foremost of the Kurus, lies the finest of maces, deposited there by King Yuvanāśva after slaying his foes in battle — decorated with golden spots, heavy, able to bear great weight, and firm."

sanskrit: sā vai śatasahasrasya saṃmitā sarvaghātinī anurūpā ca bhīmasya gāṇḍīvaṃ bhavato yathā
english: "That mace is the equal of a hundred thousand in might, a slayer of all foes, and fitting for Bhīma as the Gāṇḍīva bow is fitting for you."

sanskrit: vāruṇaś ca mahāśaṅkho devadattaḥ sughoṣavān sarvam etat pradāsyāmi bhavate nātra saṃśayaḥ ity uktvā so 'suraḥ pārthaṃ prāgudīcīm agād diśam
english: "And there is also the great conch Devadatta, of Varuṇa, with its magnificent sound. All of this I shall give you — there is no doubt of it." Having said this, that asura set out in the north-eastern direction from Pārtha.

sanskrit: uttareṇa tu kailāsaṃ mainākaṃ parvataṃ prati hiraṇyaśṛṅgo bhagavān mahāmaṇimayo giriḥ
english: To the north of Kailāsa, toward Mount Maināka, stands the holy mountain with golden peaks, great and studded with precious gems.

sanskrit: ramyaṃ bindusaro nāma yatra rājā bhagīrathaḥ dṛṣṭvā bhāgīrathīṃ gaṅgām uvāsa bahulāḥ samāḥ
english: The beautiful lake called Bindu is there — where King Bhagīratha, having seen the Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā, dwelt for many years.

sanskrit: yatreṣṭvā sarvabhūtānām īśvareṇa mahātmanā āhṛtāḥ kratavo mukhyāḥ śataṃ bharatasattama
english: It is where the great-souled Lord of all beings, having sacrificed, gathered a hundred foremost sacrificial rites, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yatra yūpā maṇimayāś cityāś cāpi hiraṇmayāḥ śobhārthaṃ vihitās tatra na tu dṛṣṭāntataḥ kṛtāḥ
english: There the sacrificial posts are made of jewels and the fire altars of gold — arranged there for beauty, not built as mere imitations of the usual pattern.

sanskrit: yatreṣṭvā sa gataḥ siddhiṃ sahasrākṣaḥ śacīpatiḥ yatra bhūtapatiḥ sṛṣṭvā sarvalokān sanātanaḥ upāsyate tigmatejā vṛto bhūtaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: It is where the thousand-eyed Śacīpati, having sacrificed there, attained perfection; where the eternal Lord of all beings, the sharp-blazing one, having created all the worlds, is worshipped, surrounded by thousands of creatures.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇau brahmā yamaḥ sthāṇuś ca pañcamaḥ upāsate yatra satraṃ sahasrayugaparyaye
english: Where Nara and Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Yama, and Sthāṇu as the fifth attend a sacrificial session at the turn of every thousand yugas.

sanskrit: yatreṣṭaṃ vāsudevena satrair varṣasahasrakaiḥ śraddadhānena satataṃ śiṣṭasaṃpratipattaye
english: Where Vāsudeva performed sacrificial sessions for thousands of years with constant faith, for the upholding of the code of the righteous.

sanskrit: suvarṇamālino yūpāś cityāś cāpy atibhāsvarāḥ dadau yatra sahasrāṇi prayutāni ca keśavaḥ
english: Where Keśava set up sacrificial posts garlanded with gold and altars blazing brilliantly, and gave there thousands upon millions in gifts.

sanskrit: tatra gatvā sa jagrāha gadāṃ śaṅkhaṃ ca bhārata sphāṭikaṃ ca sabhādravyaṃ yad āsīd vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ kiṃkaraiḥ saha rakṣobhir agṛhṇāt sarvam eva tat
english: Going there he took up the mace and the conch, O Bhārata, and the crystal hall-material that had belonged to Vṛṣaparvan; together with his attendant demons he took all of it.

sanskrit: tad āhṛtya tu tāṃ cakre so 'suro 'pratimāṃ sabhām viśrutāṃ triṣu lokeṣu divyāṃ maṇimayīṃ śubhām
english: Having brought all that, the asura built that peerless assembly hall — celebrated in the three worlds, divine, made of jewels, and auspicious.

sanskrit: gadāṃ ca bhīmasenāya pravarāṃ pradadau tadā devadattaṃ ca pārthāya dadau śaṅkham anuttamam
english: He then presented the foremost mace to Bhīmasena, and gave to Pārtha the incomparable conch Devadatta.

sanskrit: sabhā tu sā mahārāja śātakumbhamayadrumā daśa kiṣkusahasrāṇi samantād āyatābhavat
english: That hall, O great king, had pillars made of refined gold; it extended ten thousand kiṣku in every direction.

sanskrit: yathā vahner yathārkasya somasya ca yathaiva sā bhrājamānā tathā divyā babhāra paramaṃ vapuḥ
english: Blazing as fire, as the sun, and as the moon, that divine hall bore the most magnificent form.

sanskrit: pratighnatīva prabhayā prabhām arkasya bhāsvarām prababhau jvalamāneva divyā divyena varcasā
english: As though rivalling with its radiance the brilliant lustre of the sun, it shone, blazing as if with a divine, celestial splendour.

sanskrit: nagameghapratīkāśā divam āvṛtya viṣṭhitā āyatā vipulā ślakṣṇā vipāpmā vigataklamā
english: Resembling a mountain or a cloud, it stood encompassing the sky — vast, broad, smooth, free from sin, free from fatigue.

sanskrit: uttamadravyasaṃpannā maṇiprākāramālinī bahuratnā bahudhanā sukṛtā viśvakarmaṇā
english: Furnished with the finest materials, garlanded with walls of gems, rich in jewels and in wealth, beautifully built by Viśvakarmā.

sanskrit: na dāśārhī sudharmā vā brahmaṇo vāpi tādṛśī āsīd rūpeṇa saṃpannā yāṃ cakre 'pratimāṃ mayaḥ
english: Neither the Sudharmā of the Dāśārhas nor that of Brahmā was endowed with beauty comparable to the peerless hall that Maya built.

sanskrit: tāṃ sma tatra mayenoktā rakṣanti ca vahanti ca sabhām aṣṭau sahasrāṇi kiṃkarā nāma rākṣasāḥ
english: There, as directed by Maya, eight thousand rākṣasas called kiṃkaras both guarded and served that hall.

sanskrit: antarikṣacarā ghorā mahākāyā mahābalāḥ raktākṣāḥ piṅgalākṣāś ca śuktikarṇāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Moving through the sky, terrible, huge of body, immensely powerful, with red eyes or tawny eyes, with ears like shells, and wielders of weapons.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ nalinīṃ cakārāpratimāṃ mayaḥ vaiḍūryapatravitatāṃ maṇinālamayāmbujām
english: Within that hall Maya made a matchless lotus pond, with lapis-lazuli leaves spread out and lotuses of crystal stems.

sanskrit: padmasaugandhikavatīṃ nānādvijagaṇāyutām puṣpitaiḥ paṅkajaiś citrāṃ kūrmamatsyaiś ca śobhitām
english: Filled with lotus flowers and water lilies, thronged with many kinds of birds, its beauty enhanced by blooming lotuses, and adorned with tortoises and fish.

sanskrit: sūpatīrthām akaluṣāṃ sarvartusalilāṃ śubhām mārutenaiva coddhūtair muktābindubhir ācitām
english: With excellent access to its banks, unpolluted, holding water good in every season, auspicious, and sprinkled with pearl-drops tossed up by the wind alone.

sanskrit: maṇiratnacitāṃ tāṃ tu ke cid abhyetya pārthivāḥ dṛṣṭvāpi nābhyajānanta te 'jñānāt prapatanty uta
english: Some kings who came near that floor, set with gems and jewels, even on seeing it did not recognise it for what it was, and out of ignorance fell into it.

sanskrit: tāṃ sabhām abhito nityaṃ puṣpavanto mahādrumāḥ āsan nānāvidhā nīlāḥ śītacchāyā manoramāḥ
english: Around that hall on all sides grew great trees always in flower, of various kinds, blue-green, with cool shade, enchanting to the mind.

sanskrit: kānanāni sugandhīni puṣkariṇyaś ca sarvaśaḥ haṃsakāraṇḍavayutāś cakravākopaśobhitāḥ
english: Fragrant groves and lotus pools on every side, populated with geese and ducks, beautified by cakravāka birds.

sanskrit: jalajānāṃ ca mālyānāṃ sthalajānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ māruto gandham ādāya pāṇḍavān sma niṣevate
english: The wind, bearing the fragrance of garlands of water-born and land-born flowers from every direction, fanned the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: īdṛśīṃ tāṃ sabhāṃ kṛtvā māsaiḥ paricaturdaśaiḥ niṣṭhitāṃ dharmarājāya mayo rājñe nyavedayat
english: Having built such a hall and completed it within fourteen months, Maya presented it to the king Dharmarāja.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ praveśanaṃ cakre tasyāṃ rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ayutaṃ bhojayām āsa brāhmaṇānāṃ narādhipaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira made his formal entry into that hall; the lord of men fed ten thousand brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: ghṛtapāyasena madhunā bhakṣyair mūlaphalais tathā ahataiś caiva vāsobhir mālyair uccāvacair api
english: With clarified-butter porridge and honey, with sweetmeats and roots and fruits, and also with unwashed garments and garlands of every kind.

sanskrit: dadau tebhyaḥ sahasrāṇi gavāṃ pratyekaśaḥ prabhuḥ puṇyāhaghoṣas tatrāsīd divaspṛg iva bhārata
english: The lord gave each of them thousands of cows individually; there arose a cry of "puṇyāha!" that touched the very sky, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vāditrair vividhair gītair gandhair uccāvacair api pūjayitvā kuruśreṣṭho daivatāni niveśya ca
english: With various musical instruments and songs, with fragrances of every kind, the foremost of the Kurus worshipped and installed the divinities.
